Voters in Brazil today have reelected 80-year-old
President Lula da Silva to the country's highest office.
Lula defeated Flavio Bolsonaro,
the son of the country's former president

Lula is a vocal critic of President Trump,
and Bolsonaro had campaigned on a platform

Lula's election is considered an upset

he finished second to Bolsonaro,

In Michigan, President Trump called the Democratic candidate
for the U.S. Senate their Abdul Al Syed,
a jihadist at a rally in support
of the Republican candidates in the state.
Itai Samtrich Bar from member station Michigan Public reports.
The attack has become something of a closing argument
in Michigan's Senate race.
Republican candidate Mike Rogers recently released an ad
saying Al Syed supports terrorists
and is, quote, "funded by people who finance Hamas."
Independent fact checkers have rejected those claims.
During the event, President Trump brought the father
of a man killed during the September 11th
terror attacks on stage.
He repeatedly called Al Syed Mohammed

He would be the only senator that will have to go
through a metal detector before he's allowed
to go into the Senate.
I want him to have a metal detector.
The Al Syed campaign called the remarks fear-mongering.
For NPR News, I'm Itai Samtrich Bar in Port Huron.
The Justice Department is planning
to send 1,000 election monitors across the country
for the midterm elections.
NPR's Windsor Johnston reports some states say
they'll keep a close watch on them.
The Justice Department says its monitors
will protect voting rights and help prevent intimidation.
It also denies plans to send armed agents to polling places.
Oregon Secretary of State Tobias Reed
says federal observers must follow state rules.
They have to sign our observer agreement
and agree to abide by the rules laid out in that document.
Other states are also setting boundaries.
Maine and Nevada have issued guidance
on federal observers' limited authority.
Minnesota deployed state employees
to shadow federal monitors during its primary.
California has launched a similar program.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.

This is NPR.

to try and block the certification
of the Alaska U.S. Senate race

citing the fact that there's a second candidate
on the ballot with the same name.
Oysters are critical to the health of the Chesapeake Bay,
located in the Mid-Atlantic between Maryland and Virginia,
over harvesting has decimated their ranks.
But Eri Daniel reports one man
is working to bring them back.
John Consoli of Eastern Maryland marvels at these mollusks.
I think I'm more enthusiastic

He started by growing them off his pier.
Oh, this one's heavy.
Hold on, this is what I need my son, hold on.

It teaches me just how something

Consoli estimates his networks helped add
well over a million oysters back to the Bay.
For NPR News, I'm Eri Daniel.
In Ohio, Democratic Congresswoman,
who is also a member of the
Kennedy Center Board of Directors,
is asking a federal judge to demand the Trump White House
turnover documents concerning the operation
of the DC Arts Center.
Congressman Joyce Beatty is challenging
President Trump's plan to shut the Kennedy Center down
for two years for renovations.
She says records will show that Trump has been
in near constant contact
with the Kennedy Center management.
I'm Dan Roman, NPR News, Washington.
